name: Pregnancy-Associated Mortality
description: This dataset contains records of pregnancy-associated deaths, organized by year, with each row reporting a count of deaths for a combination of cause-of-death classification, racial or ethnic group, and borough. It distinguishes between deaths where pregnancy was a related factor and deaths attributed to an underlying cause, and it includes a numeric deaths column giving the count for each combination. With 236 sampled rows and six columns, the data supports analysis of how pregnancy-associated mortality varies over time and across racial and ethnic groups and geographic areas. It could be used to identify disparities, track trends, compare borough-level patterns, and examine differences between related and underlying causes of death.

name: Pregnancy-Associated Mortality

Each row reports a count of deaths for a given year, broken down by whether the death was pregnancy-related, the underlying cause of death, the decedent's race and ethnicity, and the borough of residence. Many rows use "All" in a category to represent totals across that dimension, so the data can be read at different levels of aggregation.

The related field distinguishes pregnancy-related deaths from those that were pregnancy-associated but not related, as well as cases that could not be determined. Underlying causes include mental health conditions (including overdose), cardiovascular conditions, infection/sepsis, and other categories. Race and ethnicity groups include Black non-Latina, Latina, White non-Latina, and Asian/Pacific Islander, and boroughs cover the Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Staten Island, and citywide totals. name: Pregnancy-Associated Mortality
description:
This dataset records pregnancy-associated deaths in New York City across multiple years, with counts broken down by year, pregnancy-relatedness, underlying cause of death, race and ethnicity, and borough of residence. Each row represents a death count for a specific combination of these attributes, and many rows use an "All" category to provide aggregate totals alongside subgroup breakdowns. The data span years from 2016 through 2022, with death counts ranging from 0 to 26 per row.

The dataset supports analysis of maternal mortality trends over time, disparities in outcomes by race and ethnicity, leading causes of pregnancy-associated death such as mental health conditions, cardiovascular conditions, and infection, and geographic variation across the five boroughs. It could be used for epidemiological research, health equity assessment, and planning or evaluating maternal health programs and policy. Users should note that rows mix aggregate and subgroup records, so filtering on the "All" categories is necessary to avoid double-counting.

name: Benefits and Programs API (Historical)
description:
This dataset is a historical snapshot of New York City benefits and social service programs, with 5,000 sampled rows and 34 columns. Each row describes a program, service, benefit, or resource, including its name, acronym, plain-language name, category (such as education, cash and expenses, health, work, family services, and housing), and the government agency that runs it. It also records who the program serves, such as children, families, immigrants, veterans, or youth, along with age groups and population details.

Much of the content is written for the public. Program descriptions, brief excerpts, eligibility rules, and "heads up" notes are included, often as HTML-formatted text. The dataset covers how to apply through several channels: online, by mail, in person, and by phone, with call-to-action labels, application URLs, PDF form links, and office location links where available. name: Benefits and Programs API (Historical)
description:
This dataset is a historical catalog of government benefit and social service programs, with each row representing a program, service, benefit, or resource. It covers 86 distinct programs across 12 categories, including education, cash and expenses, health, work, family services, and housing, administered by agencies such as the NYC Department of Education, NYC Housing Authority, and federal housing agencies. Each record includes the program name, acronym, plain-language name and description, category, government agency, population served, and age group, along with a page type indicating whether the entry is a program, service, benefit, or resource.

The data also documents how people access these programs. Fields capture plain-language eligibility summaries, application steps for online, mail, in-person, and phone channels, application URLs and PDF forms, required documents, and help options such as 311, email, and office locations. Most records are in English, with a small share in Spanish, and a date field indicates when each record was captured

name: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission authorized Dispatch Service Providers (DSP)
description: This dataset lists businesses authorized by the NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission as Dispatch Service Providers (DSPs). Each record represents one licensed provider and includes its license number and licensee name, along with alternate names, a full business address (building, street, secondary address, city, state, ZIP code, and borough), and a telephone number. Records also carry a last-updated date and time and a set of geographic identifiers: latitude and longitude, community board, community council, census tract, building identification number (BIN), borough-block-lot number (BBL), and neighborhood tabulation area (NTA). The sample is very small, with only two rows, so it illustrates the structure rather than the full population of providers. The data could be used to locate and map licensed dispatch providers, join them to other NYC geographic datasets for neighborhood-level analysis, contact providers, or track changes to the licensed provider list over time.

name: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission authorized Dispatch Service Providers (DSP)
description: This dataset lists businesses authorized by the NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission to operate as Dispatch Service Providers (DSPs). Each row represents one licensed provider, identified by a license number and licensee name, along with its business address (building, street, suite, city, state, ZIP code, borough) and telephone number. The records also include geographic and administrative details such as latitude and longitude, community board and council districts, census tract, NTA neighborhood name, and building and lot identifiers (BIN and BBL), plus a last-updated timestamp. The sample is very small (two providers, both in Queens), so it illustrates the schema rather than the full registry. It could be used to look up licensed dispatch providers, map their locations, join them to other NYC geographic datasets by BBL, BIN, or census tract, or analyze the distribution of providers across boroughs and neighborhoods.

name: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission authorized Dispatch Service Providers (DSP)
description:
This dataset lists Dispatch Service Providers (DSPs) authorized by the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission. Each row represents one licensed provider and includes its license number, business name, alternate name (where available), full mailing address, telephone number, and the date and time the record was last updated. It also provides geographic identifiers for each location, including latitude and longitude, borough, community board and council, census tract, building identification number (BIN), borough-block-lot (BBL), and neighborhood tabulation area (NTA).

The sample is small, with only two providers, both located in Queens, so it is best suited to illustrating the structure of the licensing data rather than supporting broad statistical analysis. It could be used to map the locations of licensed dispatch providers, examine which neighborhoods they serve, support regulatory oversight and licensing records, or join with other NYC geographic datasets using the BIN, BBL, census tract, or NTA fields.

name: ENDGBV: The Intersection of Domestic Violence, Race/Ethnicity and Sex
description:
This dataset contains 5,000 sampled records on domestic violence incidents, focusing on how victim and suspect race/ethnicity and sex intersect with offense characteristics and neighborhood economic conditions. Each row represents a single reported incident and includes the offense type, report date, police precinct code, borough name, and a flag indicating whether the parties were in an intimate relationship. Victim and suspect details cover race, sex, and reported age. Neighborhood context is captured through community district identifiers and socioeconomic measures: poverty rate, median income, and unemployment.

Because the data combine incident-level demographics with area-level economic indicators, the dataset supports analyses of disparities in domestic violence reporting and offense patterns across racial, ethnic, and gender groups, and how those patterns vary with neighborhood poverty and income. It could be used for public safety research, resource allocation, policy evaluation, or exploratory dashboards. Users should note that the file is a 5,000-row sample rather than a complete incident record, and that ages are self-reported.

name: ENDGBV: The Intersection of Domestic Violence, Race/Ethnicity and Sex
description:
This dataset contains records of domestic violence incidents reported in New York City, focused on how domestic violence intersects with race/ethnicity and sex. Each row represents a single reported incident, with details on the offense type (mostly domestic incident reports, plus smaller shares of felony assault and rape), the report date (concentrated in late December 2021), the police precinct and borough where it occurred, and whether the incident involved an intimate relationship. Victim and suspect characteristics are included where available: race, sex, and reported age. Victim records are predominantly female (about 72%) and Black (about 51%), with White, Other, and Asian/Pacific Islander groups also represented; suspect records skew male (about 67%). Missing values are common for demographic fields, especially age (about 21% missing for victims and 31% for suspects).

Most of the remaining columns describe the building's connectivity infrastructure and provider access: the number of carriers, availability of coax cable, fiber, and satellite or fixed wireless connections, fiber distribution, internet service providers (two ISP fields), multiple points of entry, designated and additional telecom space, riser space for current and additional providers, diverse riser locations, signed points of entry, agreements, and new service providers. name: WiredNYC – Certified Buildings
description:
This dataset lists 51 Manhattan office buildings certified under the WiredNYC program, which rates commercial properties on their broadband and telecommunications infrastructure. Each row represents one building and includes its name, street address, BBL (borough-block-lot) identifiers, and certification class (Platinum, Gold, or Silver). The remaining fields describe connectivity and telecom readiness: the number of carriers and internet service providers serving the building, whether fiber and coaxial cable connections are available, the extent of fiber distribution across floors, satellite or fixed wireless availability, the number and diversity of riser spaces, points of entry, designated telecom space, and whether agreements and support for new service providers are in place. A list of specific provider names is also included. Geographic fields cover latitude and longitude, community board and council district, census tract, building identification number (BIN), neighborhood tabulation area, and ZIP code.

name: WiredNYC – Certified Buildings
description:
This dataset lists New York City commercial buildings certified under the WiredNYC program, which rates properties on their broadband and telecommunications infrastructure. Each row represents one building and includes its name, street address, borough, and certification class (Platinum, Gold, or Silver). It also records connectivity details such as the number of internet service providers and carriers available, whether fiber and coaxial cable connections are present, fiber distribution across floors, satellite or fixed wireless availability, and the presence of telecom space, riser capacity, multiple points of entry, and signed points of entry. Geographic fields include latitude, longitude, community board, council district, census tract, NTA neighborhood, and postcode. The sample covers 51 Manhattan buildings, most of them Platinum-certified with five or more carriers and full or partial fiber distribution.

The data can help tenants and businesses compare connectivity options when evaluating office space, let brokers and economic development groups benchmark buildings, and support research or policy analysis on broadband infrastructure across neighborhoods.

name: DYCD Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Demographics and Services (Local Law 86)
description: This dataset contains demographic and service information for New York City's Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) programs, reported under Local Law 86. Each row covers a given year and demographic group (such as age, gender, race/ethnicity, or sexual orientation), broken down by category, with counts for crisis services and transitional independent living (TIL) services. The paired columns (crisis_services and crisis_services_1, til and til_1) appear to hold related counts or comparison values for each service type. With roughly 539 sampled rows and seven columns, the data supports analysis of which youth populations use crisis shelters versus longer-term transitional living programs, year-over-year trends in service demand, and demographic disparities in access to homeless youth services. It would be useful for program planning, policy evaluation, equity analysis, and public reporting on youth homelessness in New York City.

name: DYCD Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Demographics and Services (Local Law 86)
description:
This dataset contains demographic and service-use information for youth served by New York City's Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) programs, reported under Local Law 86. Each row pairs a fiscal year (FY18 through FY26) with a demographic breakdown—such as age at enrollment, gender, race, or sexual orientation—and a specific category within that breakdown (for example, ages 16–17 or 18–20). For each combination, the data reports counts and percentages for two service settings: crisis services and transitional independent living (TIL) programs. A separate demographic grouping covers dispositions for youth who have exited a program.

The data can be used to track how the characteristics of youth entering RHY services shift over time, compare the populations served by crisis versus transitional living programs, and identify which age, gender, race, or orientation groups make up the largest shares of clients. It supports reporting and oversight of youth homelessness services, trend analysis across fiscal years, and equity-focused review

name: DYCD Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Demographics and Services (Local Law 86)
description:
This dataset contains demographic and service-usage figures for New York City's Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) programs, reported by the Department of Youth and Community Development under Local Law 86. Each row pairs a fiscal year (FY18 through FY26) with a demographic dimension—such as age at enrollment, gender, race, or sexual orientation—and a specific category within it, then reports counts and shares for two service streams: crisis services and transitional independent living (TIL). Counts appear in the crisis_services and til columns, with corresponding percentages in crisis_services_1 and til_1. A separate demographic grouping covers dispositions for youth who have exited a program, capturing outcomes rather than participant characteristics.

The data can be used to examine which youth populations access shelter and housing services, compare the reach of crisis services versus transitional living programs, and track how service use and participant demographics shift across fiscal years. It supports policy analysis, program planning, and reporting on youth homelessness services

name: Constituent Services
description: This dataset contains records of constituent service cases handled by a city government office, with 1,274 sampled rows and 13 columns. Each row represents a single case and includes the constituent's contact ID, city, state, and postal code, along with the responsible council member and community board. Case details cover a case ID, case type, sub-types, and case subject, plus the case start and end dates and its current status. The data can be used to analyze the volume and types of requests residents submit, compare caseloads across council members and community boards, track how long cases take to resolve, and assess open versus closed cases. It supports reporting on service demand by neighborhood and identifying common constituent concerns.

name: Constituent Services
description:
This dataset records constituent service cases handled on behalf of residents, likely by a New York City council office. Each row represents one case and includes a case ID, case type (such as Housing, NYCHA, Social Services, or Quality of Life), a more specific subtype and subject (for example, rent arrears, repairs, or security deposits), the case start date, an optional end date, and the case status (Closed, Pending, or Urgent). Rows also include the constituent's contact ID, city, state, and postal code, along with the responsible council member and community board. Most constituents are in New York (state code NY), and the most common case types are Housing and NYCHA. This dataset records constituent service requests handled by a city government, with each row representing a case tied to a contact, a council member, a community board, and a location. It includes 1,274 sampled rows and 13 columns covering contact and case identifiers, city, state, postal code, council member name and district number, community board number, case type and subtype, case subject, start and end dates, and case status.

Most records are located in New York (NY), with postal codes concentrated in Manhattan-area ranges. Housing is the most common case type (about 40%), followed by NYCHA (about 23%) and Other (about 12%). name: AIR_LOT_POLYGON
description: This dataset contains 116 polygon records representing air lots, a type of property interest in which development rights above a parcel are separated from the land beneath it. Each record includes a unique object ID, model and elevation information, free-text notes, and audit fields showing who created or last edited the feature and when. Geometry measures (shape area and shape length) are included, along with parent parcel identifiers: borough, block, lot, and BBL (borough-block-lot number). Each air lot also has its own air lot number and air lot BBL, allowing it to be linked back to the underlying tax lot. The data could support mapping and analysis of air rights, property ownership and subdivision research, urban planning studies, and joining air lot records to parcel-level datasets for land use or real estate analysis.

name: AIR_LOT_POLYGON
description:
This dataset contains 116 polygon records representing air lots in New York City, with 16 attributes describing each lot's geometry, location, and administrative metadata. Each record includes a unique object ID, a model designation (mostly "D"), elevation values ranging from 10 to 1,000 feet, and notes indicating most records were created after a 2023 DTM (digital terrain model) implementation. Spatial fields capture polygon area and perimeter length, while parent location fields identify the associated borough, block, lot, and BBL (borough-block-lot) number. A separate air lot number and air lot BBL distinguish these parcels from their parent tax lots. Records also include creation and last-edit timestamps and the email addresses of the users who created or modified them.

name: AIR_LOT_POLYGON
description:
This dataset contains 116 polygon records representing air lots in New York City—three-dimensional property subdivisions above or below the surface, such as development rights transferred over a neighboring parcel. Each record links an air lot to its parent tax lot through borough, block, lot, and BBL identifiers, and includes elevation, a model code (D or B), notes, and standard GIS fields such as shape area and shape length. Records also carry creation and edit metadata (user and timestamp).

The data supports mapping and analysis of air-lot subdivisions and development-rights transfers, zoning and land-use review, and density or development-potential studies. Because air lots can be joined to parent tax-lot records via BBL, the dataset is also useful for real estate and planning research that combines property geometry with ownership or assessment data.

name: MTNYC_PlantedBlocks_20150930
description: This dataset contains records of planted street blocks in New York City, sampled at 5,000 rows with eight fields. Each row identifies a physical block (physicalid, bphys_id, objectid) and includes the street name label (stname_lab), borough code (boroughcod), segment length (segmentlen), a block-level score or classification (b5_sc), and a planting season indicator (plnt_seas). The data supports mapping and analysis of where street-tree planting activity occurred, comparing planting coverage across boroughs and streets, and examining how planting relates to block length or season. It could be useful for urban forestry planning, environmental equity studies, and neighborhood-level reporting.

name: MTNYC_PlantedBlocks_20150930
description:
This dataset contains records of street segments in New York City where tree planting occurred, organized by planting season. Each row represents a street segment and includes identifiers for the physical segment and object, the street name, borough code, segment length, and several numeric codes that likely link to planting or block-level records. The planting season field covers 17 distinct seasons, with the most common being Spring 2012, Fall 2008, and Spring 2014. Borough codes indicate that most records fall in one borough (code 4, about 68% of rows), followed by code 1 (25%), with smaller shares in codes 5 and 2.

The data could be used to analyze the geographic and temporal distribution of street tree planting across the city, compare planting activity by borough or season, and examine how segment length relates to planting locations. It could also support urban forestry planning, environmental equity studies, or mapping of planting sites when joined with street or borough reference data.

name: MTNYC_PlantedBlocks_20150930
description:
This dataset contains records of planted blocks or street segments in New York City, likely tied to street trees or urban planting sites. Each of the 5,000 sampled rows represents a single planting location, identified by physical and object IDs, a street name label, a borough code, the length of the street segment, and the planting season in which it was recorded. Planting seasons span 17 values such as Spring12, Fall08, and Spring14, indicating records collected across multiple years. Street segment lengths range widely, from roughly 10 to 2,030 units, with a typical segment around 345 units.

name: FY2013 PMMR Agency Performance Indicators
description:
This dataset contains agency performance indicators from the FY2013 Performance Management and Reporting (PMMR) system, covering New York City government agencies. Each row represents a single performance measurement for a specific agency, indicator, and reporting period, with fields identifying the agency, indicator name and sequence, sub-indicator details, desired direction of improvement, critical flags, geography, measure type, and fiscal year. Values are stored in multiple formats, including raw values, percentages, numbers, currency, time, and ratios, along with conditional formatting information.

The data can be used to track and compare agency performance across indicators, identify critical or underperforming measures, analyze trends by measure type or geography, and support budget or management decisions. It is also useful for building dashboards, conducting cross-agency benchmarking, and researching how city services are measured and reported.

name: FY2013 PMMR Agency Performance Indicators
description:
This dataset contains performance indicators reported by New York City agencies as part of the Fiscal Year 2013 Preliminary Mayor's Management Report (PMMR). Each row represents a single measurement for an agency indicator, such as the number of food stamp applications processed, the share of inspected apartments with violations, or the time taken to complete a service. Records span fiscal years 2010 through 2014, with most rows covering 2012 and 2013.

Key fields identify the agency, indicator name and ID, sub-indicator, and the type of record (an indicator value or an inquiry). Measures are stored in multiple value columns depending on their format: raw numbers, percentages, currency amounts, and time durations. Supporting fields describe the desired direction of improvement (up, down, or neutral), whether an indicator is flagged as critical, the geography covered (often citywide), and the measure type (target, actual PMMR result, total, rank, or share of inquiries).

name: FY2013 PMMR Agency Performance Indicators
description:
This dataset contains performance indicators reported by New York City agencies for fiscal year 2013, drawn from the Mayor's Management Report (PMMR). Each row represents a specific agency indicator and includes the agency name, indicator ID and name, sequence ordering, optional sub-indicator details, record type (indicator or inquiry), desired direction of improvement, critical flag, geography, measure type (such as target, PMMR result, total, rank, or percent of inquiries), and fiscal year. Reported values appear in multiple formats: raw numbers, percentages, currency amounts, and time durations, with a raw value field and format type indicating how each measure should be read.

The data covers municipal service delivery and agency accountability across dozens of agencies and geographies, including citywide totals. It could be used to track agency performance against targets, compare indicators across agencies and geographies, identify critical or underperforming measures, and build dashboards or analyses of local government operations and outcomes.

name: 2019 High Volume FHV Trip Records
description: This dataset contains a sample of 5,000 trip records for high-volume for-hire vehicles (FHV), such as rideshare services, from 2019. Each row represents a single trip and includes the license number of the operating company, the dispatching base number, pickup and dropoff timestamps, pickup and dropoff location IDs, and a shared-ride flag. The location IDs correspond to taxi zones, allowing trips to be mapped to geographic areas. With this data, users can analyze trip patterns by time of day, day of week, or location, examine travel durations between zones, compare activity across dispatching bases, and study the prevalence of shared rides. It is useful for transportation planning, congestion analysis, and research on rideshare demand.

name: 2019 High Volume FHV Trip Records
description:
This dataset contains a 5,000-row sample of 2019 trip records for high-volume for-hire vehicles (FHV), such as app-based ride services operating in New York City. Each row represents a single completed trip and includes the vehicle license number, the dispatching base number, pickup and drop-off timestamps, and pickup and drop-off taxi zone location IDs. A shared-ride flag (sr_flag) is also included but is populated for only about 23% of rows, with all recorded values equal to 1.

The data supports analysis of trip timing and duration, demand patterns by time of day, and origin-destination flows between zones. It can be used to map popular pickup and drop-off areas, compare activity across licensed operators and dispatching bases, estimate travel times, and study shared-ride usage. Because the file is a sample rather than the full 2019 record set, it is best suited for exploration, visualization, and prototyping rather than precise volume counts

description:

Each row represents a single trip and includes the vehicle operator's license number, the dispatching base, pickup and drop-off timestamps, pickup and drop-off location IDs, and a shared-ride flag.

name: Summer Sports Experience and "Kids in Motion" Programming: 2022 to current
description: This dataset records participation in New York City summer sports programs from 2022 to the present, covering both the Summer Sports Experience and "Kids in Motion" offerings. Each row captures a single session or activity, identified by borough, park or playground location, and date, along with the sports played, which program the session belonged to (KIM or SSE), attendance figures, and whether the session was cancelled. With roughly 5,000 sampled rows across seven columns, it supports analysis of attendance patterns by borough, park, sport, and program over time, comparisons between the two program types, and tracking of cancellations. It is useful for recreation planning, evaluating program reach and popularity, identifying underserved areas, and reporting on seasonal participation trends.

name: Summer Sports Experience and "Kids in Motion" Programming: 2022 to current
description: This dataset records scheduled sessions for two New York City recreation programs, Summer Sports Experience (S.S.E) and Kids in Motion (K.I.M), from 2022 to the present. description: This dataset records summer sports programming and "Kids in Motion" sessions run at New York City parks and playgrounds from 2022 to the present. Each row represents a scheduled session and includes the borough, the specific park or playground, the date and time, the sport played, the program type (K.I.M for Kids in Motion or S.S.E for Summer Sports Experience), attendance, and any cancellation reason. The data covers five boroughs and 161 locations, with sports including basketball, flag football, soccer, pickleball, and mixed "Various Sports" sessions. Attendance ranges from 0 to over 1,500 participants per session, and cancellations are logged for reasons such as bad weather, staff call-outs, or reassignment to other events. name: Broadway Curb Cut Survey Data
description:
This dataset contains field survey records documenting curb cuts along Broadway, with 1,156 sampled rows and 13 columns. Each record identifies a location by two cross streets (street_1 and street_2) and describes the condition and features of the curb ramp there, including whether a curb cut exists, ramp width, slope in inches, and whether there is no curb cut or a center cut. It also captures accessibility and maintenance details such as lip or bump measurements in inches, crumbling concrete, whether damage led to a pothole, the presence of detectable warnings, and object barriers or barriers above the ramp.

The data could be used to assess sidewalk and curb ramp accessibility, prioritize repairs and maintenance, map problem locations along Broadway, and support planning or compliance work by city agencies and advocates.

name: Broadway Curb Cut Survey Data
description:
This dataset records field survey observations of curb cuts along Broadway, one of the main streets in a city corridor. Each row corresponds to a surveyed curb cut at a Broadway intersection, identified by the cross street (street_2) and a location code (curb_cut) such as NW1, NE2, or SW1, which indicates the corner and position of the cut. With 1,156 sampled rows and 13 columns, the data captures physical condition and accessibility features of each ramp.

Most columns describe measurements or observed defects. Slope is recorded in inches (slope_inch), ramp width in inches (ramp_width), and lip or bump height in inches (lip_bump_measurement_in_inches). Condition fields flag problems such as crumbling concrete, whether damage led to a pothole, and the presence of object barriers or overhead obstructions like sewers or broken asphalt. name: Broadway Curb Cut Survey Data
description:
This dataset contains field survey records of curb cuts along Broadway, documenting accessibility features and physical conditions at each surveyed location. Each row represents one spot, identified by the primary street (Broadway) and a cross street, and records the curb cut designation (such as NW1 or NE2), ramp slope and width measurements, whether a curb cut is absent, and whether a center cut is present. It also captures defects and hazards, including lip or bump measurements, crumbling concrete, potholes, detectable warning surfaces (or their absence), object barriers, and barriers above the ramp such as drainage or broken asphalt. Many fields are sparsely populated, reflecting the variability of what surveyors observed at each site.

The data supports mapping and prioritizing curb ramp repairs, assessing accessibility for pedestrians with mobility impairments, planning capital improvements, tracking maintenance needs, and supporting ADA compliance reporting or public transparency around sidewalk infrastructure.

name: Bridge Ratings
description:
This dataset contains inspection and condition records for 3,204 bridges, with 20 fields describing each structure. It identifies bridges by a unique bridge identification number (bin) and includes location details such as borough (boro), latitude and longitude coordinates, and community district codes (cd, cd2, cd3). Descriptive fields capture what each bridge carries (feature_carried) and crosses (feature_crossed), whether a railroad is involved, the bridge type, ownership status, and number of spans.

Condition information includes the rating source, inspection date, general recommendation, current numeric rating, and a verbal rating category. Physical and financial attributes cover deck area in square feet and estimated replacement cost. The data could support infrastructure condition assessments, prioritization of repair or replacement spending, mapping of bridge locations, comparisons of condition across boroughs or bridge types, and analyses linking bridge size or age-related inspection results to cost estimates.

name: Bridge Ratings
description:
This dataset contains inspection and condition records for bridges, likely in New York City given the borough codes and coordinates. Each row represents a bridge, identified by a BIN (Bridge Identification Number), with details on what the bridge carries (such as a road or pedestrian path) and what it crosses (such as a river, parkway, or railroad). The data includes bridge type, number of spans, ownership and rating source, the date of the most recent inspection, and condition measures: a numeric current rating, a verbal rating (Good, Fair, Very Good, Poor, or Closed), and a general recommendation score. Physical and financial attributes include deck area in square feet and estimated replacement cost. Location fields cover borough, latitude and longitude (available for about half the records), and community district codes.

The dataset supports bridge infrastructure analysis and asset management. It can be used to map bridge conditions by borough or district, compare ratings across bridge types and owners, identify structures in poor condition or closed, estimate

name: Bridge Ratings
description:
This dataset contains inspection and condition records for roughly 3,200 bridges, most of them in New York City based on the borough and community district fields. Each row describes a single bridge: its identifier, the borough and community district it sits in, what it carries (such as a highway, avenue, or pedestrian path), what it crosses (a creek, river, parkway, or rail line), bridge type, number of spans, and whether a railroad is involved. It also records the inspection date, the rating source (state, city, parks, private, or university), a general recommendation score, a numeric current rating, a verbal rating (good, fair, very good, poor, or closed), deck area, and estimated replacement cost. Latitude and longitude coordinates are available for about half the records.

The data supports mapping bridge conditions by borough or district, flagging structures with low ratings or urgent recommendations, comparing inspection recency, and estimating replacement costs to help prioritize maintenance and capital budgets

name: Parks Concessions
description:
This dataset contains records of concession contracts for parks, covering 5,000 sampled rows and 58 columns. Each row represents a concession agreement and includes the property and unit identifiers, the concession operator's name and status, and the business address and contact details. Contract terms are captured through permit or license start and end dates, contract sign and end dates, original contract expiration dates, and contract status.

Financial fields include monthly minimum fees for each month of the year, annual minimum fee amounts, permit or license fees, percentage fee requirements and dates, security deposit requirements, late fee percentages and grace days, due dates, and letters of credit. The data also records concession and unit types, move-in dates, gross receipt dates, capital work requirements, and additional location information, along with a geometry type field that may support mapping.

This dataset could be used to analyze concession contract terms and fee structures, track contract status and expiration timelines, compare minimum fees across months and operators, monitor compliance with payment and reporting

name: Parks Concessions
description:
This dataset records concessions operating on New York City park properties, covering restaurants, golf courses, marinas, snack bars, gas stations, pushcarts, flower sales, and similar businesses. Each row represents a concession contract or permit tied to a specific park property, with 58 fields spanning property and unit identifiers, operator names and status, contract and permit codes, addresses and boroughs, and detailed financial terms.

Key fields include monthly minimum fee amounts for January through December, annual minimum fee schedules across up to five years, permit or license fees, security deposit requirements, percentage-fee flags, and late-payment terms. Dates cover permit or license start and end, move-in, contract signing and expiration, and original contract expiration. Several fields capture administrative details such as letter-of-credit references, capital work requirements, contract status notes, and due dates. A geometry type field indicates whether a property is represented as a polygon, point, or has no geometry.

name: Parks Concessions
description:
This dataset contains records of concession contracts and permits issued for public parks, with each row representing a single concession agreement. It covers the business and regulatory side of park concessions, including the operator's name and status, concession type (such as restaurant, pushcart, golf course, marina, snack bar, or flower sales), and location details like address, city, state, and ZIP code. Contract and permit information includes start and end dates, permit numbers, contract status, and original expiration dates. Financial fields capture monthly minimum fees for each month of the year, annual minimum fee schedules, permit or license fees, security deposits, percentage fee requirements, late fee percentages, and grace periods. Some records also include notes on letters of credit, capital work requirements, and additional location details.

name: 2015-16 Guidance Counselor Reporting - Guidance Counselor Data
description: This dataset contains 2015-16 reporting data on guidance counselors at New York City public schools, organized by school building (identified by DBN code) and location type. Each row covers one school location and includes counts of total guidance counselors and social workers, broken down by full-time and part-time status, bilingual counselors, staff serving more than one location, and staff in the absent teacher reserve (ATR). It also includes 2014-15 enrollment figures and two calculated ratios: counselors plus social workers per student, and counselors only per student. With roughly 1,600 rows and 13 columns, the data supports comparisons of counselor staffing levels and student-to-counselor ratios across schools, analysis of staffing gaps or inequities, and reporting on how resources are distributed by school type or size.

name: 2015-16 Guidance Counselor Reporting - Guidance Counselor Data
description:
This dataset reports guidance counselor staffing for New York City public schools during the 2015-16 school year, with one row per school (identified by its DBN code and location name). It covers 1,644 schools across 15 location types, including elementary, middle, high, K-8, and secondary schools.

For each school, the data includes total guidance counselor counts (total_gc) and a social-work-adjusted total (total_sw_gc), along with breakdowns of staffing by full-time, part-time, bilingual, and staff serving more than one location, plus ATR counts. It also includes prior-year (2014-15) enrollment and two counselor-to-student ratio measures: one based on counselor staffing alone and one that incorporates social work staff. Many of the staffing breakdown columns use "No Data" where information was not reported, so users should treat those values as missing rather than zero.

The dataset is useful for comparing counselor staffing and caseloads

name: 2015-16 Guidance Counselor Reporting - Guidance Counselor Data
description:
This dataset provides guidance counselor staffing information for New York City public schools during the 2015-16 school year, with one row per school identified by its DBN code. Each record includes the school name and type (such as elementary, high school, middle school, K-8, or secondary), counts of total guidance counselors and social workers, and breakdowns of staff by full-time or part-time status, bilingual capability, service across more than one location, and attendance teacher roles. It also includes prior-year (2014-15) enrollment and computed counselor-to-student ratios both with and without social workers. Many staffing detail fields use "No Data" where information was not reported.

The data can be used to examine counselor caseloads and staffing levels across schools, compare counselor-to-student ratios by school type or enrollment size, identify schools relying on part-time or shared counselors, and explore equity in student-support staffing across the district.

name: DOHMH School Cafeteria Inspections (2020-Present)
description:
This dataset contains records from New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene inspections of school cafeterias from 2020 onward. Each row represents a single inspection, linking a school (identified by name, address, borough, and geographic identifiers such as latitude, longitude, census tract, community board, and council district) to the date of inspection and any violations found. Violation entries include a code, a description, and a level, along with the permittee and site type. The sample covers 5,000 rows across 25 columns.

The data can be used to track cafeteria inspection outcomes over time, compare conditions across boroughs or districts, identify schools or areas with recurring violations, and map inspection results geographically. It may also support public health research, school food safety monitoring, and transparency reporting for parents and school communities.

name: DOHMH School Cafeteria Inspections (2020-Present)
description:
This dataset contains New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) inspection records for school cafeterias from 2020 to the present, sampled at 5,000 rows. Each row represents a single inspection event at a school food service establishment, identified by an entity ID and school name, with the school's address, city, borough, ZIP code, and geographic identifiers such as latitude/longitude, community board, council district, census tract, building identification number (BIN), borough-block-lot (BBL), and neighborhood tabulation area (NTA). The data distinguishes public school cafeterias from private school cafeterias (both for-profit and not-for-profit) and records the inspection date and the date of the most recent inspection.

name: DOHMH School Cafeteria Inspections (2020-Present)
description:
This dataset contains records of health inspections of New York City school cafeterias from 2020 onward, maintained by the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Each row represents a single inspection event and includes the school's name, address, borough, ZIP code, and geographic identifiers such as community board, council district, census tract, and coordinates. Inspection details cover the date, permittee, site type (public or private school cafeteria), and any violations found, with violation codes, severity levels, and plain-language descriptions. The sample of 5,000 rows covers roughly 700 schools, with Brooklyn accounting for the largest share of inspections.

The data can be used to track inspection frequency and violation patterns across schools and neighborhoods, map food safety outcomes geographically, compare conditions by borough or district, and identify schools with recurring problems. It also supports analyses of how cafeteria conditions differ between public and private schools and over time.

name: Preferred Source Procurements FY15
description: This dataset lists procurements from fiscal year 2015 that were awarded through preferred source purchasing, with each record showing the reason or commodity/service category for the procurement and the associated contract value. With 21 rows and two columns, it provides a compact summary of how much was spent across different preferred source categories. It could be used to analyze spending patterns by procurement reason, compare contract values across commodity and service types, or support budget and procurement reporting.

name: Preferred Source Procurements FY15
description:
This dataset lists procurements made through preferred source contracts by a city government during fiscal year 2015. Each of the 21 rows pairs a category describing the type of commodity or service purchased (such as Custom Ordered Products/Services, Data Entry, Document Processing, or Film and Cameras) with the dollar value of the resulting contract. Contract values range from $20,000 to about $3.45 million, with a mean of roughly $434,000 and a median in the tens of thousands, indicating a mix of small and large awards.

The data can be used to examine how much the city spent through preferred source procurement in FY15, compare spending across categories of goods and services, and identify the largest individual contracts. It is also useful for budget analysis, transparency reporting, and benchmarking against procurement activity in other years or jurisdictions.

name: Preferred Source Procurements FY15
description: This dataset lists procurements from fiscal year 2015 that were awarded through a preferred source, meaning purchases made under preferential contracting rules. Each of the 21 records contains two fields: a reason or commodity/service category describing the basis for the procurement (for example, Custom Ordered Products/Services, Data Entry, Document Processing, or Film and Cameras) and the corresponding contract value in dollars. Contract values range from about $20,000 to roughly $3.4 million, with a mean of around $434,000. The data supports quick summaries of preferred-source spending, such as comparing contract values across categories, ranking justifications by total expenditure, or identifying which service types account for the largest awards. Because the dataset is small and limited to two columns, it is best suited for simple aggregations and exploratory overviews rather than detailed trend or vendor analysis.

name: NYC Free Tax Prep Sites
description:
This dataset lists 184 free tax preparation sites in New York City, with 72 fields describing each location and its services. Records include the provider and site name, full street address and borough, contact details such as phone and website, and map coordinates for locating the site. The data also covers accessibility (ADA status), income limits for eligibility, and which tax situations a site can handle, such as ITIN applications, amended returns, prior-year filings, AARP support, and self-employment returns. Operating hours are given for each day of the week, along with schedule exceptions and notes, plus whether appointments or walk-ins are accepted. Geographic fields include city council and community district, neighborhood tabulation area, and BBL.

name: NYC Free Tax Prep Sites
description:
This dataset lists free tax preparation sites operating across New York City, with 184 rows and 72 columns covering location, provider, services, eligibility, and hours. Each row represents one site, identified by a site key and status (nearly all active). Records include the provider organization (for example, Food Bank For New York City, AARP Tax Aide, Ariva, Urban Upbound, and Grow Brooklyn), site name, street address, unit, borough, city, and a formatted mailing address. Phone numbers and websites are included where available.

The data also describes what each site offers: income limits for eligibility, languages spoken, whether the site handles ITIN applications, service types (in person, drop-off, or assisted self-preparation), and whether it can process amended or prior-year returns, self-employment income, and AARP-related services. Appointment versus walk-in policies are noted, along with opening and closing dates for the tax season and day-by-day hours for Monday through

name: NYC Free Tax Prep Sites
description:
This dataset lists free tax preparation sites operating across New York City, with one row per site (184 rows, 72 columns). Each record identifies the provider organization and site name, full street address, borough, phone number, website, and map coordinates, along with city council and community district codes. It also captures service details: whether the site is active, ADA accessibility, income limits for eligibility, ITIN acceptance, support for prior-year and amended returns, self-employment filing, and whether clients can walk in or need an appointment. Day-by-day opening and closing hours are included, plus notes on schedule exceptions such as holiday closures.

The data can be used to build a searchable directory or map of free tax help, examine how services are distributed across boroughs and districts to spot access gaps, compare what different providers offer, or plan outreach for residents who need free filing assistance.

name: Medical Non-production for Clinic Appointments
description: This dataset records scheduled clinic appointments that did not result in a completed visit, broken down by year, facility, and court. Each row reports the number of visits alongside counts of non-production reasons: refusal, walkout, programming, barbershop, recreation, and other, plus the total number of scheduled appointments. With 277 sampled rows and 11 columns, the data supports analysis of missed-appointment patterns, comparison of non-production causes across facilities and courts, and tracking of changes over time. It could be used by administrators, researchers, or public-safety analysts to identify where and why appointments are lost and to target scheduling or outreach improvements.

name: Medical Non-production for Clinic Appointments
description: This dataset records reasons clinic appointments were not kept at correctional facilities, broken down by year, facility, and court. Each row represents a combination of year, facility, and court, with counts for scheduled appointments and various categories of non-production: refusals, walkouts, programming, barbershop, recreation, and other reasons, plus a total scheduled figure. The data covers 277 sampled rows across 11 columns, with 10 facilities and 179 courts represented. It can be used to compare missed-appointment patterns across facilities and courts, identify which non-production reasons dominate, and track changes over time. Analysts could use it to allocate clinic resources, investigate high refusal or walkout rates, or evaluate scheduling efficiency in correctional health settings.

name: Medical Non-production for Clinic Appointments
description:
This dataset records missed or non-attended clinic appointments within a correctional healthcare setting, broken down by year, facility, and court. Each row represents a combination of these groupings and includes counts for various reasons an appointment was not completed: refusal, walkout, programming, barbershop, recreation, and other. It also includes the number of visits and the total number of scheduled appointments, allowing users to compare non-attendance against overall scheduling volume.

With 277 sampled rows and 11 columns, the data covers 10 facilities and 179 courts across 37 year values. Counts vary widely—refusals range from 0 to 3,814, while total scheduled appointments range from 939 to 18,505—so the dataset supports both facility-level comparisons and identification of the most common reasons for missed appointments.

Possible uses include analyzing patterns in missed medical appointments, comparing non-production rates across facilities and courts, identifying prevalent reasons for no-shows, and supporting scheduling or resource planning

name: NYPD Sectors
description: This dataset lists New York City Police Department patrol sectors, the geographic sub-areas within each police precinct. Each row represents one sector and includes its sector identifier, the precinct it belongs to, the patrol borough, the sector's area in square miles, its Neighborhood Coordination Officer (NCO) phase, and a sector indicator code. With 303 rows and six columns, it provides a compact reference for mapping sector boundaries to precincts and boroughs and for comparing sector sizes. It can be used to look up which precinct and borough a sector falls under, analyze the geographic distribution of patrol areas, support NCO program planning by phase, or join with incident or crime data for area-level analysis.

name: NYPD Sectors
description:
This dataset lists New York City Police Department patrol sectors, the small geographic areas used for neighborhood policing. Each of the 303 rows represents one sector, identified by a code such as 100A or 101B, along with the precinct number it belongs to. The data includes the patrol borough that oversees the sector (for example PBBS, PBBX, PBMN, PBBN, or PBMS), the sector's land area in square miles, and the sector letter designation (A through E, with A, B, and C most common). A field labeled nco_phase records the Neighborhood Coordination Officer program phase assigned to the sector, with values ranging from 1 to 99; a small number of rows are missing this value.

The dataset could be used to map and compare patrol coverage across boroughs and precincts, analyze how sector size varies within and between patrol commands, or study the rollout of neighborhood policing by phase. It could also support workload or resource analyses that

name: NYPD Sectors

Each record includes a sector identifier (such as 100A or 101B), the precinct number it falls within, the patrol borough it belongs to (for example PBBS, PBBX, or PBMN), the sector's land area in square miles, its Neighborhood Coordination Officer (NCO) phase, and a sector indicator letter (A through E). The data covers 303 sectors across the city, with sector sizes ranging from about 0.08 to 8.06 square miles.

The dataset supports mapping and spatial analysis of patrol boundaries, comparing sector sizes within and across precincts and boroughs, and linking incident or crime data to specific sectors. It can also be used to study the rollout of neighborhood policing programs through the NCO phase field, and to inform research or planning on police resource allocation and coverage.

name: Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Daily Census
description: This dataset provides a daily census of Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) programs, recording bed capacity and vacancy counts for each date. It contains 5,000 sampled rows with five columns: the date of the record, the type of program, the number of vacancies per day, the number of beds per day, and the number of vacant beds per day. The data can be used to track shelter capacity and utilization over time, compare availability across program types, identify periods of high or low demand, and support planning or reporting on youth housing services.

name: Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Daily Census
description:
This dataset provides a daily census of beds and vacancies in Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) programs, broken out by date and program type. Each row records, for a given day and program category, the number of beds available (beds_per_day), the number of vacancies (vacancies_per_day), and a vacancy rate (vacant_per_day, ranging from 0 to 1). Program types include Crisis Shelters, Crisis Shelters (HYA), Transitional Independent Living (TIL), and Transitional Independent Living (HYA). The data spans many distinct dates, with bed counts ranging from 10 to 495 per day and vacancy rates averaging about 18%.

The dataset could be used to track bed availability and utilization over time, compare capacity and vacancy patterns across program types, identify periods of high or low demand, and support planning or reporting on shelter and transitional living resources for homeless youth.

name: Runaway and Homeless Youth (RHY) Daily Census
description:
This dataset is a daily census of runaway and homeless youth (RHY) services, recording bed capacity and vacancy across shelter and housing programs over time. Each row represents one program type on one date and includes the date, the program type (Crisis Shelters, Crisis Shelters (HYA), Transitional Independent Living (HYA), or Transitional Independent Living (TIL)), the number of beds available that day, the number of vacancies, and the share of beds that were vacant. The data spans 1,388 distinct dates, with bed counts ranging from 10 to 495 per program-day and vacancy rates from 0 to 1.

The dataset can be used to track shelter capacity and utilization trends, compare occupancy across program types, and identify periods of high demand or low use. It supports resource allocation and planning for youth housing services, and can help evaluate how well emergency and transitional programs meet demand for homeless youth.

name: Small Business Services (SBS) Equal Employment Opportunity (EO 50) Certified Businesses
description:
This dataset lists small businesses certified under New York City's Equal Employment Opportunity (EO 50) program, which recognizes firms that commit to fair hiring and employment practices. Each record includes the business name, phone number, and EO 50 approval date, along with its street address, city, state, ZIP code, and borough. Geographic identifiers such as latitude and longitude, community board, council district, building identification number (BIN), borough-block-lot (BBL), 2020 census tract, and 2020 neighborhood tabulation area allow the listings to be mapped and linked to other local data.

The data can be used to find EO 50-certified businesses by location or neighborhood, analyze how certification is distributed across boroughs and council districts, support outreach or procurement programs that favor certified firms, and join with other business or demographic datasets for research and planning.

name: Small Business Services (SBS) Equal Employment Opportunity (EO 50) Certified Businesses
description:
This dataset lists businesses certified under New York City's Equal Employment Opportunity (EO 50) program, administered by the Department of Small Business Services. Each row represents one certified business, with 1,317 records and 16 fields covering the business name, phone number, street address, city, state, and ZIP code, along with the date the EO 50 approval was granted. For businesses located in New York City, the data also includes geographic identifiers such as borough, latitude and longitude, community board, council district, building identification number (BIN), borough-block-lot (BBL), 2020 census tract, and 2020 neighborhood tabulation area (NTA). Roughly half the records include these location fields, and most of those are in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens, with smaller shares in Staten Island and the Bronx.

name: Sandy Inundation Zone
description: This dataset contains 492 records identifying areas affected by Sandy-related inundation, organized by state. Each record includes a comments field for notes or context, a state designation, a demsource field indicating the elevation or digital elevation model source used, a unique id, a status field, a sourcedata field describing the origin of the underlying information, and a verified field indicating whether the record has been checked. The data could support environmental and coastal risk analysis, mapping of flood-prone zones, validation of inundation models against source documentation, and quality-control workflows that rely on verification status. It may also be useful for researchers, planners, and GIS analysts comparing inundation extents across states or tracing the provenance of mapped boundaries.

name: Sandy Inundation Zone
description: This dataset contains 492 records defining the final, field-verified high-resolution inundation zone from Hurricane Sandy in New York State. Each row represents a mapped extent of storm surge, clipped to a 1,000-foot buffer around the state's High Speed Information Program (HSIP) road network. The data was derived from New York City OEM 1-meter elevation data and source observations including USGS mission assignments, high-water marks, and surge sensors. All records share the same state, status, source, and verification values, so the dataset functions as a single authoritative boundary layer rather than a multi-variable table. It is useful for mapping Sandy's flood footprint, assessing road and infrastructure exposure, supporting emergency planning and risk communication, and serving as a reference layer in GIS analyses of coastal flood risk.

name: Sandy Inundation Zone

Each of the 492 sampled rows represents a mapped inundation zone in New York, with metadata describing how the zone was produced. The fields include the state, the elevation data source (New York City OEM 1-meter), the mapping status (Final Field-Verified High Resolution), the source data (USGS Mission Assignment, high-water marks, and surge sensors), a verification flag (Yes), and a descriptive comment. An ID column is present but holds a constant value of zero across all rows.

Because the attributes are uniform in this sample, the dataset functions primarily as a spatial layer of Sandy surge extent rather than a multi-variable table. name: Mayor’s Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence  Resource Directory
description:
This dataset is a directory of 306 social service resources compiled by a mayor’s office focused on domestic and gender-based violence. Each row describes one organization or program, with 35 fields covering its name, address, borough, ZIP code, and geographic identifiers such as latitude and longitude, community board, council district, census tract, and neighborhood tabulation area. Contact details include phone, fax, TTY, website, and hotline numbers, along with hotline and program hours. The directory also records which boroughs each resource serves, languages available for interpretation and services, wheelchair accessibility, whether fees apply, and the types of specialized and general services provided, including any additional services noted in free-text fields.

The data could be used to build searchable referral tools or service maps for people seeking help with domestic or gender-based violence, to analyze the geographic distribution of resources across boroughs and districts, to identify gaps in accessibility, language coverage, or service types, and to support planning and outreach

name: Mayor’s Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence  Resource Directory
description:
This dataset is a directory of 306 organizations and programs in New York City that provide services related to domestic and gender-based violence, compiled by the Mayor's Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence. Each row describes one resource, such as a police precinct domestic violence unit, a Safe Horizon office, a community center, or a supervised visitation program.

name: Staten Island Ferry Ridership Counts
description: This dataset contains daily ridership counts for the Staten Island Ferry, broken out by terminal. Each row records a date along with the number of riders counted at the Whitehall Terminal (Manhattan) and the St. George Terminal (Staten Island). With roughly 2,900 rows, it provides a multi-year time series suitable for tracking ridership trends, comparing directional demand between the two terminals, identifying seasonal or weekday patterns, and assessing the effects of events, weather, or service changes on ferry usage.

name: Staten Island Ferry Ridership Counts
description:
This dataset contains daily ridership counts for the Staten Island Ferry, recorded separately at its two terminals: Whitehall Terminal in Manhattan and St. George Terminal in Staten Island. Each row represents one date, with the date field stored as a timestamp string and two numeric columns giving the number of riders counted at each terminal that day. The data covers roughly 2,900 days, with about 2.5% of terminal counts missing. name: FY 2017 PMMR Data Extract
description:

The data supports finding nearby services, comparing hours and contact options, filtering by borough or walk-in availability, and building referral directories or maps for veterans seeking assistance.

Most records also indicate whether walk-ins are accepted, and some include an email address, website, and a short description of the specific services provided.

name: Future Floodplain 2020s
description:

Join and origin fields link features back to their source data.

The data can support flood risk assessment, land-use and zoning review, insurance and permitting analysis, emergency planning, and environmental studies. Each row represents one certified vendor and includes its account number, formal name and DBA, contact person, phone, website, business description, and full mailing and physical addresses. name: Restrictive Declaration Sites
description: This dataset lists 28 sites subject to restrictive declarations, with each row representing one site and its associated geographic, administrative, and property details. Fields include identifiers such as objectid and gispropnum, location information such as address, ZIP code, borough, community board, council district, police precinct, and park district, plus acreage and waterfront status. It also records legislative and jurisdictional context, including commission, acquisition, jurisdiction, property name, type category, and the state assembly, state senate, and U.S. congressional districts, along with comments, a pipratable value, and developer information. The data could support recreation and land-use planning, mapping and analysis of restricted sites by district or borough, and research into how restrictive declarations relate to property characteristics and political boundaries.

name: Restrictive Declaration Sites
description: This dataset lists 28 restrictive declaration sites in New York City, mostly privately owned waterfront parcels set aside as public access areas under restrictive declarations. Each record identifies the site by property name, GIS property number, location description, borough, community board, council district, police precinct, ZIP code, and state and federal legislative districts. It also includes acreage, waterfront status, jurisdiction (all listed as private), and the developer associated with the site. A flag indicates whether the site is rated in the city's park inspection program, and a comments field notes rating status or boundary issues. Several columns, including commission and acquisition fields, are entirely empty, and a few entries contain spelling variants of "restrictive declaration." The data could support planning and oversight work, such as mapping public-access waterfront sites, tracking which parcels are subject to restrictive declarations, identifying responsible developers, or analyzing the geographic and political distribution of these sites across boroughs and districts.

name: Restrictive Declaration Sites
description: This dataset lists restrictive declaration sites in New York City: privately held parcels, mostly waterfront, that are subject to legal deed restrictions affecting their use, often as public access or open space. Each of the 28 records includes a property name, location description, borough, acreage, and a flag for whether the site is in the city's park property database, along with the developer associated with it. Records also carry geographic identifiers such as community board, council district, police precinct, ZIP code, and state assembly, state senate, and congressional districts, making the data easy to map or join with other city datasets. Several fields, including commission and acquisition details, are entirely empty, and a few type labels contain spelling variants. The data could support mapping and analysis of restricted open space, planning and compliance reviews of land use and development, research on how deed restrictions shape waterfront access, and public transparency around individual sites and their developers.

name: 2009 - 2010 Class Size - School-level Detail
description:
This dataset provides school-level class size detail for New York City public schools for the 2009–2010 school year. Each row describes a group of classes at a particular school, broken down by grade, program type, and subject or service category, with counts of classes and students and measures of average, smallest, and largest class size. It also includes borough and community school district identifiers, school codes and names, the data source, and a schoolwide pupil-teacher ratio.

The data can be used to compare class sizes across schools, districts, and boroughs; to examine differences by grade level, program type, and subject; and to identify schools or class groupings with unusually large or small classes. It supports research on resource distribution and equity, school-level reporting, and analyses linking class size to other education outcomes.

name: 2009 - 2010 Class Size - School-level Detail
description:
This dataset provides school-level class size detail for New York City public schools for the 2009–2010 school year. Each row describes a class offering at a specific school, identified by borough (boro), community school district (csd), school code, and school name. Rows are further broken out by grade level, program type (general education, collaborative team teaching, special education, or gifted and talented), and, for middle and high school grades, core subject and course (e.g., English, math, social studies, science, algebra, living environment). For kindergarten through grade 9, a service category field captures staffing ratios such as 12:1:1.

The main measures are the number of classes, total student register, average class size, and the size of the smallest and largest classes. It also notes whether a site visit occurred and describes the structure type, establishment details, and parking-space requirements.

The data includes administrative fields such as application status, community board, council district, and 2019 installation and removal flags, along with geographic identifiers: latitude and longitude, postcode, census tract, BIN, BBL, neighborhood tabulation area (NTA), and a geocoded location field. name: Street Seats (2014 - 2019)
description:
This dataset records street seat installations in New York City from 2014 to 2019, covering 24 sampled locations. Each row represents one street seat site and includes the borough, the business or organization hosting the seat, the applicant, the year, and the street address. It also captures details about the physical setup, such as whether the seat is on a platform or sidewalk, its design type (custom or standard), and its dimensions. Parking and street-cleaning regulations at each site are noted, along with application status and site visit dates.

The data includes geographic identifiers—latitude, longitude, postal code, council district, census tract, building identification number (BIN), borough-block-lot (BBL), and neighborhood tabulation area (NTA)—making it possible to map and analyze the locations. description:
This dataset records street seat installations in New York City between 2014 and 2019. Street seats are outdoor seating areas placed in parking spaces or on sidewalks, typically associated with nearby businesses or community organizations. Each row describes one installation, including the borough, the establishment and applicant involved, the street address and cross street, the type and dimensions of the seating structure, parking regulations at the site, application status, site visit dates, and 2019 installation and removal dates. Rows also include geographic identifiers such as latitude and longitude, postal code, community board, council district, census tract, BIN, BBL, and neighborhood (NTA), along with a mapped point location.

The data can be used to map where street seats were installed and how their placement varied across boroughs and neighborhoods. name: 2015-16 Demographic Data - Admissions Methods
description: This dataset lists New York City public schools with their demographic and admissions information for the 2015–16 school year. Each row identifies a school by its DBN (District Borough Number) code and name, along with the admissions methods it uses, such as screened, audition, zoned, or lottery-based admission. With roughly 1,571 rows and three columns, it provides a compact reference for comparing how schools select or admit students. It could be used to analyze the prevalence of different admissions approaches across schools, to group or filter schools by admissions type, or to join with other school-level datasets for research on enrollment patterns, equity, or school choice.

name: 2015-16 Demographic Data - Admissions Methods
description:
This dataset lists New York City public schools and the admissions methods they used for the 2015-16 school year. Each row pairs a school's district-borough-number code (dbn) and name with a text label describing its admissions method, such as "ES: Choice District" for elementary schools admitting students by district-wide choice or "MS: Screened" for middle schools using screened admissions. With roughly 1,570 rows and 109 distinct admissions method labels, the data covers elementary, middle, and other school types across the city.

The dataset is useful for analyzing how schools select or admit students, comparing admissions approaches across districts or school levels, and mapping which schools rely on choice, screening, or other methods. It could support research on school choice policy, equity in admissions, or planning for families navigating enrollment, and it can be joined to other school-level datasets via the dbn identifier.

name: 2015-16 Demographic Data - Admissions Methods
description:
This dataset lists New York City public schools for the 2015-16 school year along with the admissions methods they use. Each row identifies a school by its district borough number (DBN) and school name, and records one admissions method associated with that school. Because schools can use more than one method, the same school may appear in multiple rows, which is why there are 1,571 rows but only 1,567 distinct school names. Admissions methods are labeled by school level and type, such as "ES: Choice District" for elementary district choice or "MS: Screened" for screened middle school admissions, with 109 distinct method labels in total. The data is nearly complete, with no missing DBNs or admissions methods and only a handful of missing school names.

name: Resident Economic Empowerment and Sustainability (REES) for NYCHA Residents – NYCHA Development - Local Law 163
description:
This dataset reports on the Resident Economic Empowerment and Sustainability (REES) program for New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) residents, broken down by NYCHA development and year, as required by Local Law 163. Each row corresponds to a NYCHA development within a borough and includes resident counts and average wages tied to REES services, such as residents served, residents placed in jobs, and related employment outcomes. The 13 columns include year, development name, borough, and multiple resident and wage measures, though several column names are duplicated or truncated, so the exact meaning of each count should be confirmed against the source data dictionary.

The data can be used to compare economic empowerment and employment outcomes across NYCHA developments and boroughs, track changes over time, and identify developments with lower placement rates or wages for further support. It is useful for city agencies, housing advocates, researchers, and community organizations studying resident employment and workforce program performance.

name: Resident Economic Empowerment and Sustainability (REES) for NYCHA Residents – NYCHA Development - Local Law 163
description: This dataset reports annual outcomes from the Resident Economic Empowerment and Sustainability (REES) program for residents of New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) developments, published under Local Law 163. Each row covers one NYCHA development in a given year from 2018 through 2024, with roughly 2,400 rows across 361 developments. Fields include the development name, borough, and counts of residents served in various program categories, such as residents enrolled, residents placed in jobs, and other participation measures. Several columns report the average wage of residents in those categories, given as dollar figures. Many counts are suppressed for privacy and appear as "< 5" or "<5" rather than exact numbers, and a substantial share of values are missing, particularly for borough (about 42%) and the wage and count columns (roughly 26% to 90%).
