name: Raised Crosswalk Locations
description:
This dataset records locations of raised crosswalks, likely as part of a transportation safety or traffic-calming program. Each of the 159 sampled rows includes a treatment type (mostly "Raised Crosswalk," with a small number of variants such as leg-specific or mid-block crosswalks), a date, a node identifier, and point geometry given as both WKT and x/y coordinates. The coordinates appear to be in a projected local system rather than latitude and longitude. A few records have missing node IDs or geometry values.

The data can be used to map and inventory raised crosswalks, examine where and when they were installed, compare treatment types across locations, and support pedestrian safety studies, planning, or GIS analysis of street infrastructure.

name: A Foundation Report: Family Violence
description:
This dataset is an annual report on family violence, organized by year and community district or borough. Its 74 sampled rows and 46 columns break down reported family-related offenses, including felony assault, rape, and homicide, and further disaggregate them by the victim's relationship to the offender (child, parent, other relative, or unknown). Additional columns capture homicide victim sex, whether there was a prior domestic incident, and the method used (blunt object, sharp object, firearm, or other). A separate set of columns covers intimate partner violence homicides with similar breakdowns, and another group records counts of family justice center clients and the services they received, such as safety planning, counseling, civil legal help, and permanent housing assistance.

The data could support analyses of how family violence patterns vary across districts and over time, comparisons between family and intimate partner violence, examination of relationship types and methods involved in homicides, and assessment of service use among family justice center clients relative to reported incidents.

name: A Foundation Report: Family Violence
description:
This dataset is a 2018 foundation report on family violence in New York City, broken down by community district and borough. It contains 74 rows and 46 columns. The main records cover the five boroughs (Brooklyn, Queens, Bronx, Manhattan, and Staten Island) and 25 community district categories, including an "Unknown" and a "Total" entry.

The data could support mapping geographic patterns of family violence, comparing incident types and victim-offender relationships across neighborhoods, examining homicide circumstances, or assessing demand for victim services.

name: 2019 DOE High School Directory
description:

Basic fields include the school's DBN code, name, borough, address, phone, email, website, and transit directions, along with geographic identifiers such as latitude, longitude, community board, council district, census tract, and neighborhood tabulation area.

Academic and program information includes overview text, available courses and Advanced Placement offerings, language and English language learner programs, diploma endorsements, extracurricular activities, and PSAL sports teams. description:
This dataset is a directory of 427 New York City public high schools for the 2019 admissions cycle, with one row per school and 462 columns. It combines school profiles with admissions and performance data. Profile fields include school name, DBN code, borough, neighborhood, address, coordinates, phone, email, website, and transit directions. Academic fields cover overview text, programs offered, AP courses, language classes, English language learner programs, diploma endorsements, extracurricular activities, PSAL sports, schedule times, and total enrollment. Performance fields include graduation rate, attendance rate, college and career readiness rate, and survey-based measures of student safety and satisfaction.

A large portion of the columns describe admissions: application methods (screened, educational option, audition, zoned), eligibility rules, priority order, selection requirements such as auditions, interviews, portfolios, and test scores, plus seat counts, applicant counts, applicants per seat, and offer rates for general education and students with disabilities.

name: Adding Chemicals to Water Supply Permits
description:
This dataset lists permits issued for adding chemicals to water supplies, with 175 sampled records and 18 fields. Each row identifies a permit by number and expiration date and gives its status, along with the business name and street address (address number, street, borough, city, state, and ZIP code). Records also include geographic identifiers such as BBL, BIN, 2010 census tract, city council district, community district, and NTA code, plus latitude and longitude coordinates.

The data could be used to map where chemical-addition water supply permits are active, examine permit status and expiration patterns, compare permit activity across boroughs, council districts, or neighborhoods, and join records to other datasets using the BBL, BIN, census tract, or coordinates. It may also support public health and regulatory oversight, compliance tracking, and neighborhood-level analysis of water supply systems.

name: Adding Chemicals to Water Supply Permits
description:
This dataset lists permits issued to businesses for adding chemicals to water supplies, likely covering water treatment and disinfection services. Each row represents a permit record and includes the permit number, expiration date, and status (Current or Historical), along with the business name and its address, city, state, ZIP code, and borough. For locations within New York City, the data also provides geographic identifiers such as BBL, BIN, census tract, city council district, community district, and NTA code, plus latitude and longitude coordinates. Many records are for businesses outside NYC, and the geographic detail fields are missing for those entries.

The data could be used to track active versus expired chemical-application permits, identify which companies hold them, and map where permitted water-treatment activity occurs. It may be useful for public health and environmental oversight, regulatory compliance checks, and analyses of how permits are distributed across boroughs and neighborhoods.

name: Adding Chemicals to Water Supply Permits

This dataset contains records of permits issued for adding chemicals to water supplies, with 175 sampled rows and 18 columns. Each row represents a permit and includes a permit number, expiration date, and status (Current or Historical), along with the business name and address of the permit holder. Location fields include street address, city, state, ZIP code, and borough, with many records marked as outside New York City. For permits tied to New York City locations, the data also provides geographic identifiers such as BBL, BIN, census tract, city council district, community district, and NTA code, plus latitude and longitude coordinates.

The data can be used to map where chemical water-treatment permits are held, monitor upcoming or past expiration dates, and compare current versus historical permits. It also supports analysis of the geographic distribution of permitted businesses, identification of concentrations by neighborhood or district, and research or oversight related to public health and environmental regulation of water treatment.

name: Greater Transit Zone
description: This dataset defines the Greater Transit Zone, a geographic boundary used in housing and development planning. It contains a single sampled record with three fields: a zone identifier (gtz_qs) and the geometric length and area of the zone's boundary. The data is essentially a spatial outline of the zone rather than a table of many observations. It could be used to map the zone, calculate its size, or overlay it with housing, land-use, or transit datasets to analyze development potential and policy coverage within the area.

name: Greater Transit Zone
description:
This dataset defines a single geographic boundary labeled the Greater Transit Zone. It contains one row with three fields: a zone label (gtz_qs) set to "Greater Transit Zone," plus the boundary's perimeter length (shape_leng) and enclosed area (shape_area) in the coordinate system's native units. Because the data consists of only one polygon, it serves as a reference outline rather than a table of multiple records.

The layer is most useful as a spatial mask or overlay. Planners and analysts could use it to clip or aggregate housing, development, or parcel data to the Greater Transit Zone, to map which properties or projects fall inside the zone, or to calculate the zone's total area for density and capacity comparisons. It can also be joined to other datasets as a geographic filter when studying transit-oriented development. Users should note that the length and area values reflect the projection used and may need conversion to familiar units such as square miles or kilometers.

name: Greater Transit Zone
description:
This dataset contains a single geographic feature representing the Greater Transit Zone, a boundary area designated in housing and development policy. It has three columns: a zone label identifying the feature as the Greater Transit Zone, and two numeric fields giving the length and area of its boundary geometry (approximately 2,093,212 in linear units and 4,390,086,774 in square units). Because the dataset holds only one record, it serves as a reference boundary rather than a table of multiple observations.

The data is most useful for mapping and spatial analysis. Planners and analysts could overlay the zone with parcel, zoning, or transit network layers, measure its footprint, or use it to screen properties and projects for transit-oriented development, housing program eligibility, or other land-use policies tied to the designated area. It could also provide a base layer for visualizations or for comparing the zone against other planning boundaries.

name: 9/11 Authorized Bus Parking Permit
description:
This dataset contains records of authorized bus parking permits issued in connection with 9/11, with about 3,900 sampled rows and 22 columns. Each row represents a permit and includes the permit year, permit and reservation numbers, valid date, bus arrival time, day of week, number of buses, permit type and quantity, and vehicle type. It also captures company details such as company name, bus company name, city, state, and ZIP code, along with issue date, return quantity, return date, and condition or restriction notes.

The data could be used to analyze bus parking demand and scheduling around 9/11 events, examine permit issuance and return patterns by company or location, study arrival times and weekday trends, or support transportation planning and historical research on event-related bus operations.

name: 9/11 Authorized Bus Parking Permit
description:
This dataset contains records of authorized bus parking permits issued around the September 11 commemorations, covering permit years 2011 through 2026. Each row represents a single permit and includes the permit number, reservation number, issue date, valid date, scheduled bus arrival time, and day of week. It also records the requesting organization's name, city, state, and ZIP code, along with the number of buses and permit quantity requested.

Vehicle details include vehicle type (mostly motorcoach, with some school buses, mini-buses, and vans) and bus company name. Permit terms are captured through the permit type (all special parking permits), condition restrictions (typically requiring a paid meter receipt), and a field indicating where the receipt should be placed. Return information shows whether a permit was returned, the quantity returned, and the return date.

name: 9/11 Authorized Bus Parking Permit
description:
This dataset contains records of authorized bus parking permits issued in connection with 9/11, covering 3,914 sampled rows across 22 columns. Each record represents a permit issued to a bus company, with details including the permit year (2011–2026), permit and reservation numbers, valid and issue dates, scheduled bus arrival times, company name, city, state, and ZIP code, vehicle type (mostly motorcoach, with some school buses and mini-buses), number of buses, permit quantity, and whether the permit was returned along with the return date. It also includes condition restrictions, such as whether a paid meter receipt is required.

The data can be used to analyze permit issuance and bus traffic patterns over time, examine which companies and vehicle types participated, track permit returns and compliance with conditions, and study the geographic distribution of operators by city and state. It could also support planning, auditing, and historical research on transportation related to 9/11 events.

name: 2020-2021 Demographic Snapshot Borough
description: This dataset provides demographic snapshots of student enrollment in New York City public schools by borough for the 2020-2021 school year. Each row represents a borough and includes total enrollment along with counts by grade level, from 3K and pre-K through grade 12. It also breaks down enrollment by gender, race and ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, multiracial, Native American, and White), and counts students with disabilities, English language learners, and students in poverty. Several columns appear in paired form, likely representing counts alongside percentages or prior-year comparisons. An economic need index is included as a summary measure. The data could support analyses of enrollment patterns, demographic composition, and equity across boroughs, such as comparing the share of English language learners or students in poverty between areas, or examining how grade-level enrollment varies geographically.

name: 2020-2021 Demographic Snapshot Borough

description: This dataset reports the percentage of live births by infant sex and mother's race/ethnicity, broken down by birth year. Each row gives a birth year, the infant's sex, the mother's race or ethnicity, the number of births, and the corresponding percentage. With 184 rows and five columns, it supports analysis of how the sex ratio at birth varies across racial and ethnic groups and over time, and can be used to compare birth distributions, track trends, or build charts and tables for public health reporting.

name: Percent Live Births by Infant Sex and Mother’s Race/Ethnicity
description:
This dataset reports live births by infant sex and the mother’s race/ethnicity for each year from 2007 to 2023. Each row gives a birth year, whether the infant was male or female, the mother’s race/ethnicity group (including Non-Hispanic White, Non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, and Other), the number of births in that group, and the percentage that count represents. The sample covers 184 rows across 17 years and seven race/ethnicity categories.

The data can be used to compare birth counts and sex proportions across racial and ethnic groups over time, to track year-to-year trends, and to examine whether the share of male versus female births differs by group or period. It is useful for demographic analysis, public health reporting, and exploratory charts or dashboards on birth patterns. Because counts vary widely between groups, users should consider both the number of births and the percentage when making comparisons.

description:

For each combination, the dataset reports the number of births and the corresponding percentage, allowing users to see both raw counts and relative shares.

The data can be used to examine trends over time, such as changes in the sex ratio at birth or shifts in the demographic composition of births. It supports comparisons across racial and ethnic groups, year-over-year analysis, and descriptive statistics or visualizations for public health reporting. Researchers, analysts, and policymakers could use it for equity-focused reporting, trend analysis, and exploratory studies of birth outcomes by demographic group.

With 5,000 sampled rows and nine columns, the data supports analyses of program reach and participation trends across sites, boroughs, and time, comparisons of enrollment by gender category, and examination of adaptive class availability. An adaptive_class column is present but entirely empty. Borough is missing for about 20% of rows, and most rows have zero participants in the not-designated category.

The data can be used to track participation trends over time, compare enrollment across sites and boroughs, and identify which class types or locations serve the most swimmers. It may also support reporting on program reach and planning future session capacity.

Most rows have no missing values, though the borough field is blank for about 20% of records and the adaptive class field is entirely empty in the sample.

The data can be used to track enrollment and participation by gender across sites and boroughs, compare demand among training locations, monitor how often classes are scheduled over time, and examine the reach of adaptive swimming offerings. It also supports planning and equity analyses for public recreation programs, such as identifying underserved areas or evaluating how municipal aquatics facilities are used.
